manual.mchjong.entry.companions.name: Inviting Companions
manual.mchjong.entry.companions.page_1: Pick online friends from the lobby sidebar or Room Settings → Invite, or run /mchjong invite <player> in chat. Guests must stand within 6 blocks and accept within 60 seconds.$(br2)The host can also add bots to fill open seats. Riichi offers simple or hard bots; MCR, Sichuan, and Taiwan each provide a dedicated built-in bot.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.name: Discards & Controls
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.page_1: Click a tile in your hand to discard it. Personal Settings offers three discard inputs: Single Click, Double Click, and Select + Confirm. Shift-clicking only selects a tile without discarding; press Enter to discard.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.page_1_con: In Riichi mahjong, press R to discard while declaring riichi, or P to skip a call prompt. Chi, Pon, Kan, and wins are issued from the on-screen action buttons; press Esc to cancel your selection.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.page_2: Press V to switch between the seated and immersive views. Hold C to inspect, right-drag to look around, scroll to zoom, and press Home to reset the view.$(br2)These bindings, along with the handbook key H, can be changed in Controls. To stand up, press Esc to close the screen first, then press sneak.
manual.mchjong.entry.customization.name: Appearance & Audio
manual.mchjong.entry.customization.page_: Slot Mahjong Dye into the box to preview face and back presets; Apply commits both at once for a single dye. Vanilla dyes recolor tile backs directly.$(br2)Reprinting a whole set erases the red marks on red fives. If your rules use red dora, reapply Red Dora Dye after printing.

Personal Settings lets you adjust camera distance, draw-and-discard speed and volume. Custom riichi sticks and voices are chosen in Personal Presets.$(br2)Put custom ZIP packs in config/mchjong/presets under faces, backs, sticks, or voices. Presets download automatically when you join a server that shares them.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.name: Placing the Table
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.page_1: Clear a flat 3 × 3 area with nothing above it and a solid block directly beneath the center. Place stools two blocks away from the center on each side you intend to play on.$(br2)Lay a tablecloth first, then put a mahjong box with a complete set inside the table.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.page_2: Craft the table from matching wooden slabs and fences, and add a white carpet to make each stool. Three carpets of the same color in a row fold into a tablecloth.$(br2)Right-click the table with a cloth in hand to drape it, then right-click again to open storage and insert the box.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.name: Table Operation
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.page_1: Riichi mahjong ordinary tables are fully hands-on, close to a real table. The dealer sweeps the tiles to shuffle, then everyone drags loose tiles in front of themselves to build a wall. Once the walls are up, the dealer picks up the dice from the center and rolls to open the wall.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.page_1_con: Deal your hand by dragging highlighted tile packets toward your hand: three rounds of four tiles, then one more tile each.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.page_2: The dealer takes the extra 14th tile (the jump tile) to start; every later draw also comes from the top of the wall. Press Tab to focus the wall, Enter or Space to take tiles, and Esc to cancel a drag.$(br2)Upgrade the table at a crafting table with iron ingots, redstone dust, copper ingots, and a hopper: an automatic table then shuffles, builds walls, deals, and draws on its own.
manual.mchjong.entry.maid.name: Touhou Little Maid
manual.mchjong.entry.maid.page_1: With Touhou Little Maid installed on both the server and the client, you can assign a maid the Mahjong task. Keep an equipped table with an empty stool inside her work area, and take your seat first.$(br2)During work hours she comes over, sits down, and follows the seat assignment. Switching her task makes her stand up and frees the physical seat.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.name: High Fans
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_1: $(bold)Big Four Winds$()$(br)88 fan$(br2)Four wind pungs or kongs. Do not add Three Winds, individual wind awards, terminal/honor pungs, or All Pungs.
$(bold)Little Three Dragons$()$(br)64 fan$(br2)Two dragon pungs/kongs and a pair of the third. No Two Dragon Pungs or Dragon Pung.
$(bold)All Honors$()$(br)64 fan$(br2)Only honors. No All Pungs, Outside Hand, terminal/honor pungs, or One Voided Suit.
$(bold)Four Concealed Pungs$()$(br)64 fan$(br2)Four concealed pungs/kongs. A pung completed by discard is exposed. No All Pungs or Concealed Hand; self-draw adds Fully Concealed Hand.
$(bold)Pure Terminal Chows$()$(br)64 fan$(br2)Two 123s, two 789s, and a pair of fives in one suit. No Full Flush, All Chows, Pure Double Chow, terminal-chow pairs, or No Honors.
$(bold)Quadruple Chow$()$(br)48 fan$(br2)Four identical chows in one suit. Do not split into Triple Chow, Double Chows, or Tile Hogs.
$(bold)Four Pure Shifted Pungs$()$(br)48 fan$(br2)Four consecutive pungs in one suit. No Three Shifted Pungs or All Pungs.
$(bold)Four Pure Shifted Chows$()$(br)32 fan$(br2)Four chows of one suit shifted consistently by one or two. Do not rescore their three-chow subsets.
$(bold)Three Kongs$()$(br)32 fan$(br2)Three kongs. Add 2 for one concealed kong, 8 for two, or concealed-pung awards for three concealed kongs.
$(bold)All Terminals And Honors$()$(br)32 fan$(br2)Only terminals and honors. No All Pungs, Outside Hand, or terminal/honor-pung points.
$(bold)Seven Pairs$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)Closed seven pairs; four identical tiles can be two pairs and score Tile Hog. No Concealed Hand or Single Wait; self-draw adds Fully Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_2: $(bold)Big Three Dragons$()$(br)88 fan$(br2)Pungs or kongs of all three dragons; no Two Dragon Pungs or individual Dragon Pung.

$(bold)Greater Honors And Knitted Tiles$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)All seven honors plus seven distinct tiles from a three-suit 147/258/369 pattern. Closed; no Lesser Knitted Honors, All Types, or Concealed Hand.
$(bold)All Even Pungs$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)Pungs/kongs and pair of even numbered tiles only. No All Pungs, All Simples, or No Honors.
$(bold)Full Flush$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)One numbered suit only; no honors. Do not add One Voided Suit or No Honors.
$(bold)Pure Triple Chow$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)Three identical chows in one suit; do not also count their Shifted Pungs or Double Chow interpretations.
$(bold)Pure Shifted Pungs$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)Three consecutive pungs in one suit; do not also count a Triple Chow interpretation of those tiles.
$(bold)Upper Tiles$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)Only sevens, eights, and nines; no Upper Four or No Honors.
$(bold)Middle Tiles$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)Only fours, fives, and sixes; no All Simples or No Honors.
$(bold)Lower Tiles$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)Only ones, twos, and threes; no Lower Four or No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_3: $(bold)All Green$()$(br)88 fan$(br2)Use only 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 bamboo and Green. Full or Half Flush may also count.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_4: $(bold)Nine Gates$()$(br)88 fan$(br2)Closed 1112345678999 in one suit, winning any tile of it. No Full Flush or Concealed Hand; self-draw adds Fully Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_5: $(bold)Four Kongs$()$(br)88 fan$(br2)Four kongs and a pair; no Single Wait. Concealed portions can add concealed-kong or concealed-pung awards.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_6: $(bold)Seven Shifted Pairs$()$(br)88 fan$(br2)Closed seven consecutive pairs in one suit. No Seven Pairs, Full Flush, Concealed Hand, or Single Wait; self-draw adds Fully Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_7: $(bold)Thirteen Orphans$()$(br)88 fan$(br2)Closed: all thirteen terminal/honor kinds and a duplicate of one. Self-draw adds Fully Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_8: $(bold)All Terminals$()$(br)64 fan$(br2)Only ones and nines. No All Pungs, Outside Hand, terminal pungs, or No Honors. Independent Double Pungs may add.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_9: $(bold)Little Four Winds$()$(br)64 fan$(br2)Three wind pungs/kongs and a pair of the fourth. No Three Winds or constituent honor-pung points.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.name: Basic Fans
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_1: $(bold)Outside Hand$()$(br)4 fan$(br2)Every group and the pair contains a terminal or honor; open allowed.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_10: $(bold)Tile Hog$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)All four copies of one kind used without declaring a kong; once per kind.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_11: $(bold)Double Pung$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)Same-rank pungs/kongs in two suits; not a subset already used by Triple Pung.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_12: $(bold)Two Concealed Pungs$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)Two concealed pungs/kongs. A discard-completed pung is not concealed.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_13: $(bold)Concealed Kong$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)Declare four owned copies as a concealed kong; not also a Melded Kong.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_14: $(bold)All Simples$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)Only suited twos through eights; open allowed. No No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_15: $(bold)Pure Double Chow$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Two identical chows in one suit; do not rescore a subset of a higher chow combination.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_16: $(bold)Mixed Double Chow$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Same-rank chows in two suits; no repeated subset of a higher combination.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_17: $(bold)Short Straight$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Two chows forming six consecutive ranks of one suit.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_18: $(bold)Two Terminal Chows$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)123 and 789 in the same suit.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_19: $(bold)Pung Of Terminals Or Honors$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)A terminal or non-value wind pung/kong. Dragons score Dragon Pung instead; do not double count.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_2: $(bold)Fully Concealed Hand$()$(br)4 fan$(br2)Self-draw without exposed calls; concealed kongs allowed. No Concealed Hand or Self Drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_20: $(bold)Melded Kong$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)A discard or added kong. Do not rescore individual kongs already counted in multi-kong fans.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_21: $(bold)One Voided Suit$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)One numbered suit is absent. Flushes and other containing fans may exclude it.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_22: $(bold)No Honors$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)No honors; excluded when already covered by All Chows, All Simples, Full Flush, and similar fans.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_23: $(bold)Edge Wait$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Only waiting on 3 of 123 or 7 of 789. No other winning kind; choose only one wait fan.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_24: $(bold)Closed Wait$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Only waiting on the middle tile of a chow; not combined with other wait fans.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_25: $(bold)Single Wait$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Only waiting to complete the pair. Melded Hand, Four Kongs, Seven Pairs, and similar forms exclude it.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_26: $(bold)Self-Drawn$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Draw your winning tile. Fully Concealed Hand, Last Tile Draw, or Replacement Win excludes this point.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_27: $(bold)Flower Tiles$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)One point per revealed flower, added only after meeting the eight non-flower minimum.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_3: $(bold)Two Melded Kongs$()$(br)4 fan$(br2)Two exposed kongs score four. One exposed plus one concealed is the six-point case of this fan. Neither adds individual kong points.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_4: $(bold)Last Tile$()$(br)4 fan$(br2)Win the fourth copy when three were already public. Opponent concealed tiles and the hidden wall do not count.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_5: $(bold)Dragon Pung$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)A dragon pung/kong; excluded when covered by Two Dragons or Big/Little Three Dragons.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_6: $(bold)Prevalent Wind$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)A round-wind pung/kong. Seat Wind may also count; do not add an honor-pung point.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_7: $(bold)Seat Wind$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)A seat-wind pung/kong; combines with Round Wind when both match.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_8: $(bold)Concealed Hand$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)Win on a discard without exposed calls; concealed kongs allowed. Self-draw instead scores Fully Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_9: $(bold)All Chows$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)Four chows and a suited pair; open allowed. No No Honors. Unlike Pinfu in Riichi mahjong, a two-sided wait is not required.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.name: Middle Fans
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.page: $(bold)Pure Straight$()$(br)16 fan$(br2)123, 456, and 789 in one suit. Do not rescore their Short Straight or Two Terminal Chows subsets.
$(bold)Lower Four$()$(br)12 fan$(br2)Only one through four; no No Honors. If only one through three, score Lower Tiles instead.
$(bold)Big Three Winds$()$(br)12 fan$(br2)Three wind pungs/kongs. No constituent honor-pung points; matching round and seat winds may add.
$(bold)Mixed Straight$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)123, 456, and 789 in three different suits.
$(bold)Reversible Tiles$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)Only reversible faces: 1234589 circles, 245689 bamboo, and White. No One Voided Suit.
$(bold)Mixed Triple Chow$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)One identical-rank chow in each suit; do not split into Mixed Double Chows.
$(bold)Mixed Shifted Pungs$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)Three pungs in different suits with consecutive ranks.
$(bold)Chicken Hand$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)No other non-flower fan. Example: open, ordinary ron on 6p, with no last-copy bonus. Flowers still add.
$(bold)Last Tile Draw$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)Self-draw the last wall tile; do not add Self Drawn.
$(bold)Last Tile Claim$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)Win the discard after the last draw. This differs from Last Tile, the final copy of a kind.
$(bold)Out With Replacement Tile$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)Win a kong replacement by self-draw; no Self Drawn. Flower replacement alone does not qualify.
$(bold)Three-Suited Terminal Chows$()$(br)16 fan$(br2)123 and 789 in each of two suits, with fives of the third as pair. No All Chows, Mixed Double Chow, terminal-chow pairs, or No Honors.
$(bold)Robbing The Kong$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)Win another player’s added-kong tile; do not add Last Tile.
$(bold)All Pungs$()$(br)6 fan$(br2)Four pungs/kongs and a pair; open allowed. Higher containing patterns may exclude it.
$(bold)Half Flush$()$(br)6 fan$(br2)One numbered suit plus honors; no One Voided Suit.
$(bold)Mixed Shifted Chows$()$(br)6 fan$(br2)Three chows in different suits, shifted by one.
$(bold)All Types$()$(br)6 fan$(br2)Include all three suits, a wind, and a dragon.
$(bold)Melded Hand$()$(br)6 fan$(br2)All four groups exposed, then win the pair on a discard. No Single Wait.
$(bold)Two Concealed Kongs$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)Two concealed kongs score eight, not six. Do not add their individual kongs or Two Concealed Pungs.
$(bold)Two Dragon Pungs$()$(br)6 fan$(br2)Two dragon pungs/kongs; no individual Dragon Pung awards.
$(bold)Pure Shifted Chows$()$(br)16 fan$(br2)Three chows in one suit shifted consistently by one or two.
$(bold)All Fives$()$(br)16 fan$(br2)Every group and the pair contains a five. No All Simples or No Honors.
$(bold)Triple Pung$()$(br)16 fan$(br2)Pungs/kongs of one rank in all three suits; do not split into Double Pungs.
$(bold)Three Concealed Pungs$()$(br)16 fan$(br2)Three concealed pungs/kongs. A discard-completed pung is exposed; no Two Concealed Pungs.

$(bold)Lesser Honors And Knitted Tiles$()$(br)12 fan$(br2)Closed fourteen distinct tiles from three-suit 147/258/369 and honors. If all nine suited tiles are present, add Knitted Straight; self-draw adds Fully Concealed Hand.
$(bold)Knitted Straight$()$(br)12 fan$(br2)Nine tiles: 147, 258, 369 in different suits, plus a group and pair. Only the extra group may be open. Do not split the knitted body for other fans.
$(bold)Upper Four$()$(br)12 fan$(br2)Only six through nine; no No Honors. If only seven through nine, score Upper Tiles instead.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.name: Flowers & Winning
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_1: MCR is played by four players with 136 ordinary tiles and eight flowers: 144 in all. You start with 13 tiles, or 14 as the dealer, who discards first. Turns move counterclockwise.$(br2)Replace opening flowers dealer-first, one player at a time. Reveal each flower and replace it from the wall tail; keep replacing if another flower appears.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_2: You can chow only from the previous player; you may pung or melded-kong any opponent. Wins take priority, then pung/kong, then chow. If several players win the same discard, the closest one after the supplier wins.$(br2)Take a replacement after a concealed kong. An added kong waits for robbery responses. Flower replacement alone is not a kong-replacement win, and flowers never join groups.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_3: The regular shape is four groups and a pair. See $(l:mcr_special)Special Hands$(/l) for Seven Pairs, Thirteen Orphans, knitted forms, and Knitted Straight.$(br2)You need eight non-flower points to win. Each flower adds one afterward. Seven points plus two flowers is still short; eight points plus two flowers qualifies and pays as ten.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_4: MCR has no riichi or dora, and no Riichi mahjong furiten. Declaring a complete shape below eight non-flower points is a wrong win: pay each opponent ten and lose permission to win for this hand.$(br2)Keep drawing, discarding, and calling; the restriction clears next hand. A Win button only means the shape is complete; check fan and points before declaring.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_5: On self-draw, each opponent pays eight plus the total hand score. On a discard, the discarder pays that amount and the other two pay eight each.$(br2)For eight points plus two flowers, self-draw collects 18 each: 54. A discard collects 18, 8, and 8: 34. There is no dealer multiplier or fu.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_6: Start at zero and play sixteen hands across East, South, West, and North. The dealer moves after every hand, even a dealer win or draw. Exhaustion collects no ready payment; earlier wrong-win penalties remain.$(br2)All 81 fans appear in $(l:mcr_fan_high)High Fans$(/l), $(l:mcr_fan_middle)Middle Fans$(/l), and $(l:mcr_fan_low)Basic Fans$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.kongs: These two kongs score six if one is exposed and one concealed.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.name: Shapes & Combinations
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.page_1: Seven Pairs allows four copies as two pairs. Thirteen Orphans uses thirteen terminal/honor kinds and a duplicate. Neither accepts melds.$(br2)Honors and Knitted Tiles selects fourteen distinct kinds from three-suit 147/258/369 and honors. All seven honors makes Greater Honors. Both are closed; they exclude All Types and Concealed Hand, but self-draw adds Fully Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.page_2: Knitted Straight uses 147, 258, 369 in different suits plus one group and pair. You cannot chow the nine-tile body; only the extra group may be open.$(br2)Wait fan checks the residual shape. Tiles already allocated to the body stay out; a separate copy of the same kind may complete the residual wait.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.page_3: Add compatible fans; parts already covered by a larger fan or another arrangement score only once. A combined group may link once more with an unused group.$(br2)Mixed Triple Chow does not also give Mixed Double Chows; Pure Straight does not add its Short Straight or terminal-chow pair. Choose the best scoring interpretation; do not add the alternatives.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.page_4: Index numbers are fan values. Ordinary patterns allow open groups unless stated closed. Hong Kong tile images may show only the relevant groups; complete the hand and meet the stated circumstances.$(br2)+ marks the winning tile, / separates exposed groups from hand tiles, and ; precedes already-public tiles. Two concealed kongs score eight; a mixed pair scores six, without counting those kongs again.
manual.mchjong.entry.presets.name: Rules & Red Fives
manual.mchjong.entry.presets.page_1: The host picks a rule preset in the lobby; hover any option to read its description. Settings cover red fives, starting points, game length, and bankruptcy. Changing rules resets everyone's readiness.$(br2)Three-player mahjong drops 2m through 8m and plays with 108 tiles. North can stay in your hand as a normal tile or be extracted for an extra draw, depending on the preset.
manual.mchjong.entry.presets.page_2: One red dye crafts four Red Dora Dyes; combine one with a 5m, 5p, or 5s tile to turn it into a red five, and use Undo Dye to change it back.$(br2)Spare red fives can be stored in the box. The table picks a complete matching set automatically; every tile type still needs four usable copies, red fives included.
manual.mchjong.entry.replays.exports: Riichi, MCR, Sichuan, and Taiwan replays can all be exported to Tenhou JSON format, saved in the replays/mchjong folder in your game directory.
manual.mchjong.entry.replays.name: Reviewing Matches
manual.mchjong.entry.replays.page_1: Open the record from the table screen with the Replays button, or run /mchjong replays. Only players who took part in the match can view its replays.$(br2)Pick a finished hand and go through it on the timeline or with the play button. Arrow keys step hand by hand, Home/End jump around, and Space toggles play and pause.
manual.mchjong.entry.replays.page_2: Finished matches can be exported to JSON files and saved in the replays/mchjong folder in your game directory.$(br2)Replay the entire match at any time to review discards, decision times, riichi declarations, and win evaluations. You can pause or exit the replay at any time.
manual.mchjong.entry.results.name: Results & Leaving
manual.mchjong.entry.results.page_1: When a hand ends, settlement shows the winning score and point transfers. Riichi mahjong also lists yaku, han, and fu; multiple ron winners can be selected separately. Use the continuation button to confirm the next hand.$(br2)Ordinary tables pay with physical sticks: press E or open the side drawer, then drag sticks into the receiving player’s row.
manual.mchjong.entry.results.page_2: After settlement on an ordinary table, sweep the played tiles to the center. When the match ends, you return to the lobby and the dice and drawer sticks reset.$(br2)Solo practice against bots can always be quit in one click. Leaving a multiplayer match requires a unanimous vote, and the clock is paused while the vote is open.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi.declaration: Online riichi needs 1,000 points and at least four live tiles (three in three-player mahjong). M.League and JPML A need one live tile; WRC allows zero. Competition presets do not require 1,000 points already in hand.$(br2)Temporary furiten clears on your next draw. Riichi kans must keep your waits; see $(l:riichi_presets)Preset Differences$(/l) for further restrictions.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi.name: Riichi, Calls & Furiten
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi.page_1: Declare Riichi when you are tenpai with a closed hand: pick the tile to discard, play it, and post a 1,000-point stick. Your hand is then locked; apart from winning or a concealed kan, you can only draw and discard.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi.page_1_conti: Chi builds a sequence from the previous player's discard; Pon and Kan build triplets or quads from anyone's discard. Calling opens your hand: closed-hand-only yaku no longer count, and kuisagari yaku lose one han.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi.page_2: If any tile you are waiting on is among your own discards, you are in discard furiten and cannot ron on any of your waits. Passing a winning discard gives you same-turn furiten; after riichi it lasts until the hand ends.$(br2)You can still win by tsumo while in furiten. The red furiten badge on screen always tells you your current state.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.aborts: Online presets allow aborts. On an uninterrupted first draw, nine distinct terminals/honors lets you choose Nine Terminals. Four identical first wind discards without any call abort.$(br2)Four riichi or four kans by multiple players also abort, after the fourth kan’s replacement and discard win checks. One player’s four kans continue. Aborts carry no noten payment; dealer repeats and honba rises.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.name: From Deal to Finish
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.page_1: Four-player Riichi mahjong uses four copies of each suited tile and seven honors: 136 tiles. Everyone receives 13; the dealer takes one extra and discards first. Turns move counterclockwise.$(br2)The last 14 tiles form the dead wall for replacement draws and dora indicators. Flowers are not used.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.page_2: Start with $(l:winning)Winning Hands$(/l), then read $(l:riichi)Riichi, Calls & Furiten$(/l). Normally you need one yaku han; dora cannot supply it.$(br2)Discard after Chi or Pon. A kan uses four tiles as one group, so take a replacement. An added kan may be robbed. A concealed kan keeps your hand closed.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.page_3: The dealer repeats after winning, or after an exhaustive draw when tenpai. Otherwise the deal moves on. Draws and repeats add a honba; a nondealer win resets it.$(br2)Noten players share a 3,000-point payment to tenpai players: one receives 3,000, two receive 1,500 each, or three receive 1,000 each. All tenpai or all noten means nothing is paid.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.page_4: You normally play East and South, with four dealer positions per wind. Repeats add hands. Mahjong Soul and Tenhou also offer East-only matches.$(br2)Online presets end after settlement if someone is below zero; zero remains playable. See $(l:riichi_presets)Preset Differences$(/l) for final-dealer stops and extension.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.page_5: Each award pairs its explanation with a tile image using Kansai faces. Groups are separated by gaps; + marks the winning tile. The example illustrates a condition, not the final score.$(br2)Continue with $(l:riichi_yaku)Yaku$(/l), $(l:riichi_yakuman)Yakuman$(/l), and $(l:riichi_points)Fu & Points$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.name: Fu & Points
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.page_: Regular hands start at 20 fu. Add ten for closed ron or two for tsumo. Pinfu tsumo stays at 20 without tsumo fu; Seven Pairs stays at 25. Round other totals up to the next ten.

Simple open pung/closed pung/open kan/closed kan: 2/4/8/16 fu. Double those for terminals or honors. Ron completing a pung makes it open for fu.$(br2)Value pair: two fu, or four for online double winds. Edge, closed, or pair wait: two. Two-sided and paired waits: zero. An otherwise fu-less open hand is thirty.
Below mangan, basic points = fu × 2^(han + 2). Ron pays ×4 to a nondealer or ×6 to dealer. Nondealer tsumo charges dealer ×2 and others ×1; dealer tsumo charges each ×2. Round each payment up to 100.

A nondealer’s three han forty fu has 1,280 basic points: ron 5,200; tsumo 2,600 from dealer and 1,300 each from others. Each honba adds 300 to ron or 100 per tsumo payer. The winner takes deposits.$(br2)Two-han Seven Pairs ron is 1,600: do not round 25 fu to 30.

Mangan: five han or basic points reaching 2,000; ron 8,000 for nondealer, 12,000 for dealer. Six–seven han pays ×1.5, eight–ten ×2, eleven–twelve ×3.$(br2)Normally thirteen-plus gives counted yakuman, ×4; M.League caps ordinary hands at ×3. Natural yakuman excludes ordinary yaku/dora and can compound.

Dora follows the indicator: nine wraps to one, winds cycle East–South–West–North, dragons White–Green–Red. Each copy adds one han; red fives add another.$(br2)Riichi wins reveal ura. Kans add indicators and corresponding ura. JPML A omits ippatsu, ura, and kan dora. Bonuses never replace a qualifying yaku.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.name: Preset Differences
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.page: Mahjong Soul and Tenhou normally require one yaku han; two or four can be selected. Dora never counts, and Tenhou also excludes ippatsu from this minimum. Natural yakuman qualifies.$(br2)Open tanyao, zero/three/four reds, and East/East–South stay within these presets. Other changes are Custom.

Mahjong Soul starts/returns 25,000 in four-player and 35,000 in three-player. Uma: +15/+5/−5/−15, or +15/0/−15.$(br2)Tenhou: 25,000→30,000 or 35,000→40,000. Uma: +20/+10/−10/−20 or +20/0/−20. First also receives oka from the return/start difference. Bonuses use thousands of points.

Online presets have bankruptcy, aborts, extension, and final-dealer stops. A repeating final dealer ends if top and at target; otherwise repeat. Without a repeat, below target extends at most one wind. Targets: 30,000/40,000.$(br2)Mahjong Soul allows multiple ron; Tenhou aborts triple ron. Only Soul doubles the four special yakuman forms.

M.League: 25,000→30,000; uma +30/+10/−10/−30, oka 20. Three reds, ippatsu/ura, rounded-up mangan, ordinary hands capped at sanbaiman.$(br2)JPML A: 30,000 start/return, no reds, ippatsu, ura, or kan dora. No rounded-up mangan; counted fourfold mangan allowed. Uma depends on floating players.

JPML A floating players, then first-to-last uma:$(br)0 or 4: 0 / 0 / 0 / 0$(br)1: +12 / −1 / −3 / −8$(br)2: +8 / +4 / −4 / −8$(br)3: +8 / +3 / +1 / −12$(br2)Exactly 30,000 counts as floating. Final score is (points − return)/1000 plus uma and oka, with the preset’s tie treatment.

WRC: 30,000 start/return, uma +15/+5/−5/−15, no reds; ippatsu, ura, rounded mangan, counted fourfold limit, and alternative renhou mangan.$(br2)All three competition presets use head bump, with no bankruptcy, aborts, nagashi, extension, or final-dealer stop. Repeats remain. Tied bonuses are shared; JPML A/WRC leave final deposits unclaimed.

Rounded mangan covers four han thirty fu and three han sixty fu. Double-wind pairs: online four fu, competition two. Riichi kans keep waits; competition also keeps interpretations, and JPML A keeps yaku.$(br2)Big Dragons/Winds have liability; competition also has Four Kans. The liable player covers tsumo, usually sharing a third-party ron.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_sanma.name: Three-player Riichi
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_sanma.page_1: Three-player mahjong removes 2m–8m for 108 tiles and has no Chi. Hands still start at 13/14, with East, South, West: three dealer positions per wind.$(br2)Keep North as an ordinary tile or extract it for a replacement and one bonus han. Extraction keeps the hand closed but supplies no yaku. 1m and 9m indicate each other as dora.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_sanma.page_2: North extraction interrupts ippatsu and can be won by an eligible opponent. Its replacement alone is not Rinshan; extractions share replacement capacity with kans.$(br2)Tsumo charges the two present opponents their usual four-player shares, with no replacement for the missing share. Nondealer mangan: 4,000 from dealer, 2,000 from the other. Noten pool: 2,000.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.name: Yaku
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_1: $(bold)Riichi$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Declare with a closed ready hand and a 1,000-point deposit. The hand locks; do not add to Double Riichi.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_10: $(bold)White dragon$()$(br)1 han$(br2)A White dragon pung/kan; open allowed. Little Three Dragons also adds its two dragon yaku.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_11: $(bold)Green dragon$()$(br)1 han$(br2)A Green dragon pung/kan; open allowed. Little Three Dragons also adds its two dragon yaku.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_12: $(bold)Red dragon$()$(br)1 han$(br2)A Red dragon pung/kan; open allowed. Little Three Dragons also adds its two dragon yaku.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_13: $(bold)Rinshan kaihou$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Self-draw a kan replacement; open allowed. North replacement alone is not Rinshan.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_14: $(bold)Chankan$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Ron on another player’s added-kan tile; open allowed. Kokushi has a separate concealed-kan exception.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_15: $(bold)Haitei raoyue$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Self-draw the last ordinary live-wall tile; open allowed. A replacement is not Haitei.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_16: $(bold)Houtei raoyui$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Ron on the discard after the last ordinary draw; open allowed.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_17: $(bold)Chiitoitsu$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Seven distinct pairs, closed. A four cannot be two pairs. Fixed 25 fu; not also Ryanpeikou.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_18: $(bold)Sanshoku doujun$()$(br)2 / 1 han$(br2)Same sequence in all three suits: two han closed, one open.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_19: $(bold)Ittsu$()$(br)2 / 1 han$(br2)123, 456, 789 in one suit: two han closed, one open.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_2: $(bold)Double riichi$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Closed riichi on your first discard before any call. Replaces ordinary Riichi.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_20: $(bold)Chanta$()$(br)2 / 1 han$(br2)Every group and pair includes a terminal/honor, with a sequence and honors present. Two closed, one open.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_21: $(bold)Toitoi$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Four pungs/kans and a pair; open allowed. Seven Pairs is not All Pungs.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_22: $(bold)Sanankou$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Three concealed pungs/kans; the other group may be open. Ron completing a pung makes that pung exposed.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_23: $(bold)Sanshoku doukou$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Same-rank pungs/kans in all three suits; open allowed.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_24: $(bold)Sankantsu$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Three declared kans, open or concealed, plus the remaining group and pair.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_25: $(bold)Shousangen$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Two dragon pungs/kans and the third as pair; open allowed. Add the two dragon yaku.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_26: $(bold)Honroutou$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Only terminals and honors; open allowed. Add All Pungs for the regular shape or Seven Pairs for that shape.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_27: $(bold)Honitsu$()$(br)3 / 2 han$(br2)One numbered suit with honors: three han closed, two open.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_28: $(bold)Junchan$()$(br)3 / 2 han$(br2)Every group and pair contains a terminal, with sequences and no honors. Three closed, two open; replaces Chanta.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_29: $(bold)Ryanpeikou$()$(br)3 han$(br2)Two pairs of identical sequences, closed. Do not also score Iipeikou or Seven Pairs.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_3: $(bold)Ippatsu$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win within one uninterrupted turn after riichi. Calls, kans, and north extraction interrupt it. JPML A omits it.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_30: $(bold)Chinitsu$()$(br)6 / 5 han$(br2)One numbered suit without honors. Six han closed, five open; not also Half Flush.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_31: $(bold)Blessing of Man$()$(br)Mangan$(br2)WRC only: a nondealer ron before their first draw and before calls. Compare alternative mangan with ordinary scoring; do not add yaku or dora to it.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_32: $(bold)Nagashi mangan$()$(br)Mangan$(br2)At exhaustion, every discard is a terminal/honor and none was claimed. Usually no calls; Tenhou allows them. Pays mangan tsumo without honba or deposits.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_4: $(bold)Menzen tsumo$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Self-draw a closed hand; concealed kans allowed. Can combine with Pinfu.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_5: $(bold)Pinfu$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Closed four sequences, a non-value pair, and a two-sided wait. Twenty fu on tsumo; thirty on ron.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_6: $(bold)Tanyao$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Only suited twos through eights. Open by default; closed only when open tanyao is disabled.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_7: $(bold)Iipeikou$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Two identical sequences in a closed hand. Ryanpeikou replaces it.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_8: $(bold)Seat wind$()$(br)1 han$(br2)A pung/kan of your seat wind; open allowed. A double wind gives two han.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_9: $(bold)Round wind$()$(br)1 han$(br2)A pung/kan of the round wind; open allowed, combining with Seat Wind.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.name: Yakuman
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.page: $(bold)Kokushi musou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Closed thirteen terminal/honor kinds plus one duplicate; ordinary wait is one yakuman.
$(bold)Ryuuiisou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Only 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 bamboo and Green; open allowed. Green dragon is not mandatory.
$(bold)Chuuren poutou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Closed one-suit 1112345678999 plus one extra suited tile; no declared kans.
$(bold)Pure chuuren poutou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Exactly 1112345678999 before winning, waiting on all nine ranks. Double in Mahjong Soul, single elsewhere.
$(bold)Suukantsu$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Four declared kans and a pair, open or concealed. Declaring the fourth alone does not win.
$(bold)Tenhou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Dealer wins the initial dealt hand, closed and uninterrupted by calls.
$(bold)Chiihou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)A nondealer’s first self-draw before any call; closed only.
$(bold)Kokushi musou thirteen-sided wait$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)All thirteen kinds once before winning: thirteen-sided wait. Double in Mahjong Soul, single elsewhere.
$(bold)Suuankou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Four concealed pungs/kans, closed. A paired wait must self-draw; ron completing a pung loses this yakuman.
$(bold)Suuankou tanki$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Four concealed groups already complete, waiting for the pair. Ron allowed. Double in Mahjong Soul, single elsewhere.
$(bold)Daisangen$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Three dragon pungs/kans; open allowed. No ordinary dragon yaku. Feeding the final exposed dragon group can cause liability.
$(bold)Shousuushii$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Three wind pungs/kans with the fourth as pair; open allowed.
$(bold)Daisuushii$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Four wind pungs/kans; open allowed. Double in Mahjong Soul, single elsewhere. Feeding the fourth exposed group can cause liability.
$(bold)Tsuuiisou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Only honors; open allowed. A seven-pairs shape also qualifies.
$(bold)Chinroutou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Only suited ones and nines, in four pungs/kans and a pair; open allowed.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.name: Seating & Preparation
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.page_1: Right-click a stool to sit down; the first player to sit becomes the host. Select the variant in the lobby sidebar, then configure its player count and rules in Match settings.$(br2)Invite friends or fill empty seats with Bots. Once all seats have occupants, use the separate seat-preparation button.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.page_2: Ordinary tables deal concealed wind tiles to decide seats; automatic tables assign them directly. Sit at your assigned stool and click Ready; auto-seating is on by default.$(br2)The match starts when everyone is sitting in the right seat and ready, and the equipment matches the rules.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.name: Fan Patterns
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_1: $(bold)All pungs$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Four pungs/kongs and a pair; open allowed. Seven Pairs is not also All Pungs.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_10: $(bold)Last-tile win$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Win on the final draw or its following discard. Ready checks do not assume this fan.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_2: $(bold)Golden single wait$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Four fixed pung/kong melds, with a single tile waiting for its pair. Add All Pungs for another fan.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_3: $(bold)Full flush$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)One numbered suit, open allowed. Combines with Seven Pairs, Roots, or All Pungs, still subject to the cap.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_4: $(bold)Seven pairs$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)Seven pairs without melds. Four copies count as two pairs and also a Root; not All Pungs.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_5: $(bold)Root$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Four copies used without a declared kong, one fan each. MIL lists declared Kongs separately.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_6: $(bold)Kong$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Each declared kong in MIL adds one fan, separate from income. T/TFMJ counts it as Root instead.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_7: $(bold)Win after kong$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Self-draw after kong replacement; payment still adds the self-draw point to the resulting base value.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_8: $(bold)Shoot after kong$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Win a kong-related discard; refunds/transfers are separate. MIL also applies it to the added-kong-after-replacement case.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_9: $(bold)Robbing a kong$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Win the added fourth tile; the original pung remains. Not also shooting for that same event.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.name: Sichuan Play
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.notati: Award explanations face images using Sichuan tiles. Gaps separate groups; + marks the winning tile and / separates fixed melds from hand tiles.$(br2)Only the relevant groups may be shown. Complete the winning shape and apply the stated conditions. Values are for that award, not the whole hand. Ordinary patterns allow open groups unless stated closed.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.page_1: Sichuan is played by four players with 108 suited tiles, with no honors or flowers. You receive 13 tiles, or 14 as the dealer. Choose one suit to void after the deal; you must clear every tile of it before winning.$(br2)Discard void-suit tiles first. There is no chow. You can pung and kong only the other suits.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.page_2: MIL also asks you to secretly bind your first discard. Play that tile at your first discard turn. If you have none of the void suit, no tile is bound. All void suits are revealed together, but chosen tiles stay private.$(br2)T/TFMJ selects only the suit. Neither preset exchanges three tiles.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.page_3: Win with four groups and a pair, or Seven Pairs. No minimum fan is required. Four identical tiles may count as two pairs.$(br2)In blood battle, winners retire while everyone else keeps playing. Three winners or wall exhaustion ends the hand. Several players may win one discard; its supplier pays each separately.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.page_4: Passing a win blocks a later win of the same or lower fan, even after declining self-draw. Drawing again or becoming not ready clears it.$(br2)Compare fan after the cap. Two hands both capped at three fan remain equal even if one has more raw fan.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.page_5: Zero, one, two, and three fan pay a base value of 1, 2, 4, and 8; three fan is the cap. A discarder pays that value. Each still-active opponent pays value plus one on self-draw.$(br2)A two-fan Full Flush takes four on a discard. With all four active, self-draw takes five each, or fifteen; after one retires, it takes ten.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.page_6: The first winner deals next. If the first win has several winners on one discard, its supplier deals. With no winner, the dealer stays. Both presets normally play eight hands and rank cumulative scores.$(br2)Continue with $(l:sichuan_fan)Fan Patterns$(/l) and $(l:sichuan_payments)Kongs & Draws$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.sichua: Four copies: two pairs and a root.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_payments.pa: A concealed kong collects two from each active opponent; a discard kong collects two from its supplier. Immediately adding the drawn fourth tile to a pung collects one from each active opponent. A delayed added kong collects nothing.$(br2)Kong income is separate from winning fan. Replace after a kong; a robbed added kong does not complete or collect.

After a kong-related shooting discard, MIL refunds only the last kong to its original payers. T/TFMJ transfers the whole paid consecutive-kong chain to the winners.$(br2)If that chain earned five and two players win, each receives three; the shooter supplies the missing one. Winning payments are separate.

MIL calls declared quads Kong and undeclared fours Root; T/TFMJ calls both Root. Each adds one fan.$(br2)If an added kong after a replacement is won, MIL treats it as shooting: the kong completes without income. T/TFMJ treats it as robbery and keeps the pung. MIL has longer East/West walls; T/TFMJ has longer South/North walls.

At exhaustion, remaining not-ready players pay each eligible ready player their highest structural base value. Do not include replacement or last-tile circumstances. Not-ready players also refund retained kong income.$(br2)Ready values of two and eight cost a not-ready player two and eight. Retired winners are excluded. Three winners end without draw checks or refunds.

Keeping void tiles at exhaustion is a passive flower pig: treat it as not ready and refund kongs. A referee-called active violation deducts 24 competition points, forbids wins, and refunds kong income; that penalty pays nobody.$(br2)A sanctioned ready player neither receives nor pays ready payments. Completed call transfers stay final. Custom rules can change caps, bonuses, kong amounts, and match length.
manual.mchjong.entry.stock.name: Dice & Point Sticks
manual.mchjong.entry.stock.page_1: Ordinary tables need dice and point sticks of your own. Bone meal combined with white and black dye crafts two dice, and a bone block stonecuts into 24 blank sticks.$(br2)Dye blank sticks white, blue, yellow, red, or black to make 100-, 1,000-, 5,000-, 10,000-, and −10,000-point sticks.
manual.mchjong.entry.stock.page_2: A standard 25,000-point start calls for 17 sticks per seat: ten 100s, four 1,000s, two 5,000s, and one 10,000. A 30,000 start adds one 5,000, and a 35,000 start adds one 10,000.$(br2)Sticks can be stored in the box or the side drawer. Without bankruptcy, keep one black negative stick per seat ready for negative balances.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.name: Sixteen-tile Play
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.notatio: Award explanations face images using Taiwan tiles. Gaps separate groups; + marks the winning tile. / separates exposed groups from hand tiles, or different players in flower examples.$(br2)Only the relevant groups may be shown. Complete the winning shape and apply the stated conditions. Values are for that award, not the whole hand. Ordinary patterns allow open groups unless stated closed.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.page_1: Taiwan is played by four players. Pocket adds eight flowers to the ordinary 136; Southern omits flowers. At least one human can play with built-in Bots.$(br2)Deal four packets of four, then one extra to the dealer, who discards from 17. A regular win needs five groups and a pair, not fourteen-tile Seven Pairs or Thirteen Orphans.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.page_2: Opening flowers are replaced in dealer-first rounds; flowers drawn as replacements wait for the next round. During play, reveal and replace flowers from the tail until you draw an ordinary tile.$(br2)You may chow the previous player; pung or kong any opponent. Win takes priority over pung/kong, then chow. The nearest winning claimant after the supplier wins.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.page_3: Discard after chow or pung. All kongs take a replacement; only an added kong can be robbed. A kong itself has no immediate payment.$(br2)Declare ready with a discard that leaves you waiting. Afterward, draw and discard only: calls and kongs are locked. Ready needs no deposit and winning does not require it.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.page_4: Passing a win blocks both discard and self-draw wins. Drawing alone leaves it in place. Discard a kind outside your waits before that draw or call, or complete an added kong.$(br2)Normally reserve sixteen tiles plus one per completed kong; fixed sixteen is an option. Reserved tiles cannot replace flowers or kongs. No legal replacement means a draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.page_5: Complete sixteen dealer positions across East, South, West, and North. Dealer wins and draws add a repeat. A nondealer win moves the deal and clears repeats, including at the final North position.$(br2)Scores start at zero. There are no ready payments, abortive draws, bankruptcy, or dealer-win stops. See $(l:taiwan_payments)Flowers, Base & Tai$(/l) and $(l:taiwan_tai)Tai Patterns$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.taiwan: Five groups and a pair: seventeen.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_payments.pag: A discard win charges the discarder; self-draw charges all three opponents. Each pays base + per-tai value × payable tai. Defaults are base one and one per tai.$(br2)Pocket adds one dealer tai when either party is dealer, plus two per repeat. Southern omits the one dealer tai but keeps two per repeat.

In Pocket, a nondealer self-draw worth three tai during one repeat collects four from each nondealer and seven from the dealer: 1 + 3 + 1 + 2. Total: fifteen.$(br2)Southern caps hand tai at four before dealer/repeat additions. Its dealer winning eight raw tai during one repeat collects 1 + 4 + 2 = 7 from each liable payer.

Eight Flowers and Seven Robs One each award eight tai without a regular 17-tile win. Eight Flowers charges all three; Seven Robs One charges the lone-flower holder.$(br2)Your seventh or eighth flower waits for replacement. An opponent drawing the last lone flower triggers Seven Robs One immediately. Opening flower wins wait until all replacement rounds finish.

Flower wins are automatic and bypass ordinary passing. A regular replacement win adds its own tai. Seven Robs One charges flower tai to one payer and regular self-draw tai to all three; each owes only one base.$(br2)Pocket scores seat flowers, flower sets, and single waits; flower replacement can score Replacement Win. Southern has no flowers or Single Wait tai, kong-only Replacement Win, and a four-tai cap.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.name: Tai Patterns
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_1: $(bold)Heavenly hand$()$(br)24 tai$(br2)Dealer wins the dealt hand after flowers, before calls. No Concealed Self Draw, Concealed, Self Draw, or Replacement Win.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_10: $(bold)Full flush$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Only one numbered suit, open allowed; not also Half Flush.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_11: $(bold)Small four winds$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Three wind pungs/kongs and the fourth as pair; open allowed, with two other groups.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_12: $(bold)Big three dragons$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Three dragon pungs/kongs; open allowed. No individual dragon tai.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_13: $(bold)Five concealed triplets$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Five concealed pungs/kongs. Replaces Three/Four Concealed Triplets but still adds All Triplets. A discard-completed pung is exposed.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_14: $(bold)Four concealed triplets$()$(br)5 tai$(br2)Four concealed pungs/kongs; the other group may be open. Replaces Three Concealed Triplets.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_15: $(bold)All triplets$()$(br)4 tai$(br2)Five pungs/kongs and a pair; open allowed. Excluded by All Honors, but combines with Five Concealed Triplets.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_16: $(bold)Half flush$()$(br)4 tai$(br2)One numbered suit plus honors; open allowed.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_17: $(bold)Small three dragons$()$(br)4 tai$(br2)Two dragon pungs/kongs and the third as pair; open allowed. No individual dragon tai.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_18: $(bold)Pinfu$()$(br)2 tai$(br2)Five sequences and a suited pair, no honors or flowers, won by discard. Open allowed. Not restricted to two-sided waits; Single Wait may add.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_19: $(bold)Three concealed triplets$()$(br)2 tai$(br2)Three concealed pungs/kongs; other groups may be open. A discard-completed pung is not concealed.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_2: $(bold)Earthly hand$()$(br)16 tai$(br2)Nondealer wins their first draw before calls. No Concealed Self Draw, Concealed, or Self Draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_20: $(bold)Concealed hand$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)No exposed calls; concealed kongs allowed. Closed self-draw scores three, not one plus one.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_21: $(bold)Self-draw$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Draw the winning tile; open allowed. Concealed Self Draw replaces it when closed.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_22: $(bold)Concealed self-draw$()$(br)3 tai$(br2)Closed self-draw, concealed kongs allowed. No separate Concealed/Self Draw; Heavenly/Earthly Win excludes it.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_23: $(bold)All from others$()$(br)2 tai$(br2)All five groups exposed; win the pair on a discard. No concealed kong.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_24: $(bold)Half from others$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)All five groups exposed, self-draw the pair. Not also All From Others.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_25: $(bold)Replacement win$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win a kong replacement; Pocket also allows flower replacement. Ordinary self-draw tai may add.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_26: $(bold)Last draw$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win the last drawable tile; reserved tiles are not drawable.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_27: $(bold)Last discard$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win the discard after the last drawable tile.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_28: $(bold)Robbing a kong$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win another player’s added-kong tile; concealed kongs cannot be robbed.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_29: $(bold)Declared ready$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win after declaring ready. Heavenly/Earthly Ready replaces this tai. The declaration need not be closed.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_3: $(bold)Human hand$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Nondealer wins a supplier’s first discard before dealer’s second discard and before calls. No Concealed award.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_30: $(bold)Single wait$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)The whole hand waits on one kind, including edge, closed, or pair waits. Not one remaining physical copy. Southern omits it.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_31: $(bold)Red dragon$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)A Red dragon pung/kong, open allowed. Big/Small Three Dragons excludes it.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_32: $(bold)Green dragon$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)A Green dragon pung/kong, open allowed. Big/Small Three Dragons excludes it.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_33: $(bold)White dragon$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)A White dragon pung/kong, open allowed. Big/Small Three Dragons excludes it.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_34: $(bold)Flower set$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Complete either family of four flowers, one tai per family. Pocket also adds seat flowers; flower victories exclude these ordinary flower awards.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_35: $(bold)Round wind$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)A round-wind pung/kong, open allowed; may also be Seat Wind.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_36: $(bold)Seat wind$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)A seat-wind pung/kong, open allowed. Seat winds follow the current dealer.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_37: $(bold)Seat flower$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Flower numbers one through four match East through North; one tai per matching flower. Not added to flower victories.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_4: $(bold)Heavenly ready$()$(br)16 tai$(br2)Dealer declares ready on the first uninterrupted discard and later wins. No Concealed or Declared Ready.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_5: $(bold)Earthly ready$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Nondealer declares ready on the first uninterrupted discard and later wins. Replaces Declared Ready.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_6: $(bold)Eight flowers$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)All eight flowers force a win without a regular shape. No Seat Flower or Flower Set; a regular replacement win may add.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_7: $(bold)Seven robbing one$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Seven flowers with the eighth held by an opponent; that opponent pays. No Seat Flower or Flower Set; regular replacement scoring is separate.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_8: $(bold)Big four winds$()$(br)16 tai$(br2)Four wind pungs/kongs, open allowed, plus another group and pair. Seat/Round Wind may add.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_9: $(bold)All honors$()$(br)16 tai$(br2)Only honors; open allowed. Do not add All Triplets.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.name: Crafting a Tile Set
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.page_1: Planks, bone blocks, quartz blocks, calcite, glass, and amethyst blocks all stonecut into 16 blank tiles each; nine blocks give exactly 144 blanks, a full set.$(br2)Craft the box from leather, wooden slabs, a chest, and an iron nugget, then right-click it while holding it to open.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.page_2: Put exactly 136 or 144 blanks with matching material and backs into the tile slots. One of each black, red, green, blue, and white dye crafts Mahjong Dye.$(br2)Insert it into the dye slot, pick the face preset, and click Apply to print the whole set; the 144-tile style includes eight flower tiles.
manual.mchjong.entry.winning.name: Winning Hands
manual.mchjong.entry.winning.page_1: A standard winning shape is four groups plus one pair: 14 tiles. Groups are either sequences (three consecutive numbers of one suit) or triplets (three identical tiles). Honors can only form triplets.$(br2)Seven Pairs and Thirteen Orphans are exceptions. Winning on your own draw is tsumo; winning on another player's discard is ron.
manual.mchjong.entry.winning.page_2: To win, your hand needs at least one yaku on top of the shape (the minimum-han requirement). Start with closed riichi, All Simples, and the triplet yaku of your seat wind, round wind, and dragons. Dora adds han but never counts toward the minimum.$(br2)For practice, the host can enable Open Hands. Turn on Tenpai Hints in Room settings before starting to see your waits and remaining copies computed from the visible tiles in real time.

manual.mchjong.recommend.text: Install the optional Patchouli mod to read the Mahjong Handbook in-game. Please download the file matching your Minecraft version and mod loader.
mchjong.ponder.table_equipment.text_1: Put the tiles your rules need into the box: 136 for four players or 108 for three, all with matching material, backs, and face preset. Spare tiles may stay in the box.
mchjong.ponder.table_equipment.text_2: Right-click the table to open its storage; it holds up to two boxes.
mchjong.ponder.table_equipment.text_3: Right-click the table with a cloth in hand to drape it. With the cloth down and a full set ready, you can start preparing a match.
mchjong.ponder.table_equipment.text_4: Open the side drawer to store every stick denomination and pay players manually during settlement.
mchjong.ponder.table_equipment.text_5: While waiting, move boxes in and out through the storage screen. Keep both hands empty and sneak-right-click the tabletop to retrieve the cloth.
mchjong.ponder.table_placement.text_1: Leave a clear 3 × 3 area for the table, with nothing blocking the space above.
mchjong.ponder.table_placement.text_2: Place the table in the center of the area; its rim reaches into the surrounding blocks.
mchjong.ponder.table_placement.text_3: Put one stool two blocks from the center on each side you play on.
mchjong.ponder.table_placement.text_4: Both ordinary and automatic tables use this compact layout.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_1: Right-click a stool to sit down and open the table screen; right-click the stool again while seated to reopen it.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_2: Pick a three- or four-player preset in the lobby, then have everyone click Ready.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_3: On ordinary tables, sweep the loose tiles to shuffle, drag stacks in front of you to build the wall, then drag tiles from the wall into your hand.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_4: Automatic tables shuffle, build walls, deal, and draw all by themselves.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_5: Click a table tile to discard it. The screen lists the chi, pon, kan, riichi, and win options available right now.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_6: Close the screen and you can look around while staying seated; press sneak to stand up.
mchjong.ponder.workshop_dyeing.text_1: A mixer and basin color two targets per dye: a whole tile stack or one box each. Two boxes and one blue dye color both complete sets.
mchjong.ponder.workshop_dyeing.text_2: Only the backs change. Faces, red fives, material, names, sticks, and dice stay untouched. Glass tiles turn into tinted glass.
mchjong.ponder.workshop_dyeing.text_3: One Undo Dye removes the back color from two targets. Both must actually change; otherwise the machine stays off and the dye is not consumed.
mchjong.ponder.workshop_dyeing.text_4: A deployer applies Red Dora Dye to 5m, 5p, and 5s tiles one by one on belts or depots. Undo Dye restores them one by one, keeping the back color.
mchjong.ponder.workshop_dyeing.text_5: A mixer marks 16 identical blank sticks with a single dye: white 100, blue 1,000, yellow 5,000, red 10,000, and black −10,000 points.
mchjong.ponder.workshop_production.text_: A mechanical saw cuts 24 blank tiles from each material; six materials make 144. A bone block also yields 32 blank point sticks.
Mix black, red, green, blue, and white dye for two Mahjong Dyes. One red dye blends into eight Red Dora Dyes, and one black dye into eight Undo Dyes.
To build a box, have a deployer attach leather and an iron nugget to a chest, then press it. This route saves the wooden slabs.
Under a mechanical press, place an empty box, 144 identical blank tiles, one Mahjong Dye, and a printing plate, and the machine prints Kansai faces.
The press outputs the full 144-tile box and returns the plate. Send the plate back for the next batch; material, backs, and names are kept.
The press and basin can also pack tiles, marked sticks, and dice into a box, obeying the existing slot limits. Finished boxes can be delivered straight to the table.

rules.mchjong.option.abortive_draws.desc: Includes the mid-hand draws: nine terminals, four winds, four kans, and four riichi.
rules.mchjong.option.agari_yame.descript: Ends the match as soon as the dealer wins the final hand and reaches first place, without a dealer repeat.
rules.mchjong.option.award_final_deposit: Gives any unclaimed riichi-stick deposits left on the table to the overall winner when the match ends.
rules.mchjong.option.bankruptcy.descript: Ends the match the moment any player's points drop below 0. Being at exactly 0 keeps the game going.
rules.mchjong.option.calls_clear_furiten: Clears same-turn furiten as soon as any player makes any call.
rules.mchjong.option.compound_yakuman.de: Adds up the points of every distinct yakuman a winning hand satisfies at once.
rules.mchjong.option.delayed_open_kan_do: Flips the kan-dora indicator for open kans and added kans after the discard, not at the moment the kan is declared.
rules.mchjong.option.double_wind_pair_fu: Scores 4 fu for a pair of double winds (both round and seat wind) instead of the usual 2 fu.
rules.mchjong.option.double_yakuman.desc: Counts suuankou tanki, kokushi musou thirteen-wait, pure chuuren, and daisuushii as double yakuman.
rules.mchjong.option.extension.descripti: If no player has reached the target score when the final hand ends, the match continues into extra rounds.
Adjusts the placement bonuses according to how many players finish at or above the return points (floating).
rules.mchjong.option.floating_uma.descri: When the number of players at or above return points is %s, the placement bonus for rank %s (in points).
rules.mchjong.option.formal_tenpai_ignor: Counts a hand as tenpai at an exhaustive draw even when all of its waits are already visible.
rules.mchjong.option.head_bump.descripti: When several players ron the same discard, only the closest one counter-clockwise from the discarder wins.
rules.mchjong.option.ippatsu.description: Adds ippatsu (+1 han) for winning within one uninterrupted turn cycle after declaring riichi.
rules.mchjong.option.ippatsu_counts_towa: Lets ippatsu count toward meeting higher minimum-han requirements.
rules.mchjong.option.kan_dora.descriptio: Flips an additional dora indicator in the dead wall whenever a kan is declared.
rules.mchjong.option.kazoe_yakuman.descr: Scores a hand whose regular yaku total 13 or more han as a yakuman rather than sanbaiman.
rules.mchjong.option.kiriage_mangan.desc: Rounds 3-han 60-fu and 4-han 30-fu scores up to a full mangan
rules.mchjong.option.kuitan.description: Keeps All Simples valid after opening your hand with chi, pon, or an open kan.
rules.mchjong.option.match_length.descri: How long the match runs: tonpuusen (East only) or hanchan (East and South).
rules.mchjong.option.min_han.description: The lowest han total a win must meet, counting yaku only.
rules.mchjong.option.min_riichi_wall.des: The minimum number of drawable tiles left in the wall for riichi to be allowed (usually 4 in standard rules).
rules.mchjong.option.nagashi_allows_call: Allows your own calls without voiding Nagashi Mangan.
rules.mchjong.option.nagashi_mangan.desc: Scores Nagashi Mangan as a mangan tsumo when every discard in your river is an uncalled terminal or honor at an exhaustive draw.
rules.mchjong.option.needs_riichi_deposi: Forbids declaring riichi when holding fewer than 1,000 points.
rules.mchjong.option.pao_ron_honba_by_di: When a liable yakuman is won by ron off another player, that discarder pays the full honba bonus.
rules.mchjong.option.pao_tsumo_honba_sha: Shares the honba payment among all non-winning players when a liable yakuman tsumo compounds with a non-liable one.
rules.mchjong.option.red_fives.descripti: How many red fives go into the deck: so many 5m, 5p, and 5s each.
rules.mchjong.option.renhou_mangan.descr: Scores Blessing of Man as a mangan when you ron before your first draw, without any calls.
rules.mchjong.option.replacement_capacit: How many replacement tiles the dead wall reserves (usually 4 in four-player mahjong).
rules.mchjong.option.return_points.descr: The benchmark score for standings; when it differs from the starting points, the gap goes to first place as the oka.
rules.mchjong.option.riichi_kan_keeps_me: Forbids a concealed kan after riichi that would change how the hand's melds are drawn or interpreted.
rules.mchjong.option.riichi_kan_keeps_ya: Forbids a concealed kan after riichi that would make an existing yaku disappear.
rules.mchjong.option.rob_concealed_kan.d: Lets Kokushi Musou ron the tile an opponent declares a concealed kan with (robbing the concealed kan).
rules.mchjong.option.rob_north_without_k: In three-player mahjong, lets any non-Kokushi hand waiting on North rob an opponent's extracted North.
rules.mchjong.option.round_shared_placem: Hands out a 100-point remainder in placement calculations starting from the original dealer.
rules.mchjong.option.shared_ranks.descri: Players tied at the end split the placement and oka of the tied ranks evenly, without tiebreaking by dealer order.
rules.mchjong.option.starting_points.des: The points each player starts the match with.
rules.mchjong.option.suukantsu_pao.descr: Assigns pao liability for Suukantsu to whoever feeds the fourth kan to a player who already has three.
rules.mchjong.option.target_points.descr: The minimum score the leader must hold when the final hand ends; missing it triggers extension winds such as nishiiri or minamiiri.
rules.mchjong.option.triple_ron_draw.des: Declares the hand an abortive draw if three players ron the same discard at once.
rules.mchjong.option.uma.description: The placement bonus for rank %s in raw points (enter e.g. 10000 for +10).
rules.mchjong.option.ura_dora.descriptio: Flips the ura-dora indicators beneath the revealed dora indicators when a riichi hand wins.
rules.mchjong.option.whole_hand_pao.desc: When a liable yakuman compounds with another yakuman, the liable player pays the whole hand's yakuman points.
rules.mchjong.option.yakuless_furiten.de: Triggers same-turn furiten even when the winning tile you passed lacks qualifying yaku.
